summary: This function reads employee data from separate CSV files for each year (2020-2024), renames the salary column in each file to include the year, and merges them all together on employee identity columns. The final combined dataset is saved to a new CSV file with salary data for all years side-by-side.

explanations.1: The function accepts an optional filename parameter that defaults to 'employees', allowing you to reuse this code with different data files.
explanations.3: We read the 2020 file first and use it as our starting point; sep=';' means the CSV uses semicolons instead of commas as column separators.
explanations.4: We rename the generic 'salary' column to 'salary_2020' so it won't clash with salary columns from other years.
explanations.7: We loop through years 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024 (range(2021, 2025) stops before 2025).
explanations.15: We join the current year's data to our merged dataset using an outer join on id, first_name, and last_name — this keeps all employees even if they appear in only some years.
explanations.18: We write the final merged dataset to a CSV file with semicolon separators, using UTF-8 encoding and excluding pandas' row index column.
